extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, regulatory staff, and NRECA members/advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes policy and regulatory priorities NRECA is promoting (permitting reform, FEMA reform, funding, generation/transmission, storage, and regulatory rollbacks) to ensure reliable, affordable power for electric cooperatives and their consumer-members. Useful as background for drafting advocacy comments, congressional outreach, or agency submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite federal permitting for energy projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress must pass permitting reform legislation to give electric cooperatives the certainty they need to invest in new transmission lines and power plants to meet growing demand for power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should speed the process without changing substantive environmental standards; streamline NEPA for co-ops and reduce redundant reviews for federally funded improvement projects; House-passed examples include the SPEED Act and PERMIT Act. The page emphasizes making timelines shorter and reducing delays that increase project costs and stall construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regulatory certainty/stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Put permitting and policy rules in statute to avoid policy 'boomerangs' when administrations change so asset owners can make long-term investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory certainty is framed as necessary for capital-intensive investments with long lead times and long asset lives (30–80 years). Guidance includes advocating for statutory fixes rather than short-term policy shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure dispatchable, reliable and affordable power
rubrics_metrics.description: Electric systems must deliver dispatchable, reliable, and affordable electricity so 'the lights come on when they turn the lights on.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion underpins policy positions: support for always-available generation (nuclear, hydropower, fossil fuels where necessary), avoiding premature retirements, and investments that stabilize rates and protect consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and enable always-available generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Because solar and wind are intermittent, utilities need the ability to build nuclear, hydropower or fossil fuel plants to ensure the power stays on during non-solar periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy positions include opposing regulations that would force closures or make operating existing plants cost-prohibitive; permitting reform is presented as a mechanism to speed the construction of such generation when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit litigation delays on federal permitting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Litigation challenging federal permitting decisions should have reasonable time limits so it doesn’t delay crucial infrastructure projects for years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames reasonable time limits on challenges as part of permitting reform packages (e.g., SPEED Act goals) to reduce 'frivolous litigation' and stop multi-year project holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline NEPA application for co-ops and federal grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperatives should not have to undergo full NEPA review every time they get federal grants or other types of funding for improvement projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SPEED Act is cited as an example that would shorten timelines and reduce repetitive NEPA burdens for co-ops receiving federal support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform Clean Water Act permitting to reduce costs and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut red tape and provide greater regulatory certainty for co-ops that obtain Clean Water Act permits to lower construction costs and speed project timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PERMIT Act is presented as a package of commonsense reforms to Clean Water Act permitting processes to lower costs, speed timelines and reduce confusion for permittees.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA public assistance efficiency and loan-interest reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA’s public assistance program should be more efficient for co-ops and allow reimbursement (including interest) for recovery loans taken while awaiting FEMA funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights Category F public assistance (permanent repairs) approval as critical and advocates for the Fixing Emergency Management for Americans (FEMA) Act to speed fund delivery and reimburse interest on loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase and stabilize RUS lending authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow the Rural Utilities Service (RUS) Electric Loan Program capacity and appropriate funds so co-ops can borrow for system improvements, maintenance, resiliency and to meet growing demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA advocates for continued appropriations and expansion of annual loan authority; guidance includes demonstrating effective use of loans and the federal government's interest benefit from co-op loan interest payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support wildfire mitigation and quality vegetation management
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve co-ops’ ability to mitigate wildfire threats through quality vegetation management and support legislation such as the Fix Our Forests Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as part of resiliency and permitting priorities; the page stresses the need for tools and authority to reduce wildfire risk from vegetation near lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid regulatory rollbacks that force premature generation retirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose rules that would require co-ops to add exorbitantly expensive controls or shut down critical plants, because such rules can impose higher costs without meaningful public health benefits and harm reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repeal of the 2024 EPA mercury/air rule is cited as a win; NRECA filed comments arguing the rule was not cost-effective, legally/technically unsound, and would cause closures, job loss, and higher costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize federal infrastructure programs to improve resilience and cybersecurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with DOE and other agencies to implement infrastructure investments that make systems more resilient to disasters and enhance grid cybersecurity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA emphasizes constructive collaboration with DOE, USDA and use of programs like New ERA and bipartisan infrastructure funds to drive resilience and security improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate addition of resources to serve large loads (Speed-to-Power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speed the addition of electricity resources to serve rapidly growing, large loads (e.g., data centers) so load growth does not outpace generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include faster permitting, whole-of-government coordination, managing reliability risks of large loads, and supporting DOE's Speed-to-Power Initiative. The page notes it’s often faster to build a data center than a power plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a whole-of-government approach for large-load policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use smart, cross-government policies to help co-ops serve data centers and other large loads while protecting electricity consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA submitted comments to DOE and FERC highlighting co-ops' role in data center development and urging coordinated federal support to meet load growth without passing undue costs to members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilize rules for broadband and BEAD program participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure broadband regulatory burdens are reduced and BEAD program rules stabilize so co-ops can decide whether to participate without constantly shifting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page praises FCC efforts to reduce regulatory burden but warns repeatedly changing BEAD program rules discourages co-op participation; advocates for clear, consistent rules and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and pilot long-duration energy storage technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Test and deploy long-duration storage (e.g., vanadium redox flow batteries) as scalable, long-lived solutions to improve reliability and manage intermittency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The VRFB pilot is highlighted: advantages include scalability (independent stacks/tanks), longer life (~20 years) vs lithium-ion (~4 years), longer duration (up to 10+ hours), and multiple applications (reducing outages, stabilizing prices, backing renewables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize resource adequacy through multiple measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Address worsening resource adequacy projections by speeding resource and transmission additions, managing large-load reliability risks, coordinating electric and natural gas systems, and streamlining siting/permitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites NERC’s Long-Term Reliability Assessment: calls for industry, regulators, and policymakers to speed additions, improve coordination, and reform siting/permitting to avoid supply shortfalls in the next decade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community outreach and stakeholder engagement for projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold outreach events to gather input from community members and answer questions, which helps inform the best approach for project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIUC/AES Hawaiʻi example: multiple outreach events aided project acceptance; engagement is framed as instrumental to taking large-scale renewable projects to the finish line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify environmental benefits and offsets in project evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and publicize fossil fuel offsets and avoided emissions (e.g., gallons of fuel offset, metric tons CO2 avoided) as benefits of PPAs and renewable projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIUC projects projected offsets (179 million gallons of fossil fuel; 2.3 million metric tons CO2 avoided) are used to demonstrate life-of-PPA climate benefits and support project rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize and right-size physical grid infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Decommission outdated substations and build modern switchyards/substations to connect new solar-plus-storage and other projects to the grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: build Kaawanui Substation to connect solar-plus-storage; modernization is presented as necessary for safe, reliable interconnection of new resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and emphasize local economic/community benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how projects stabilize rates, provide jobs, improve economic activity, and support local agriculture as part of project justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proponents should highlight local economic impacts and job creation in outreach; these co-benefits can help secure community support and policy momentum.
